name: Face Illumination
description: Reconstructs per-face illumination environment maps using spherical harmonics to detect lighting inconsistencies between the synthesized face and its surrounding scene context.
mechanism:
This method analyzes facial illumination consistency for deepfake detection:

1. **Light Source Estimation**: The primary illumination direction is estimated from facial shading using shape-from-shading techniques. The face's known approximate 3D geometry (frontal face as a convex surface) constrains the lighting estimation — shadow patterns on nose, cheeks, and forehead indicate light position.

2. **Face-Scene Illumination Comparison**: The illumination direction estimated from facial shading is compared with illumination cues in the scene: background shadows, specular highlights on objects, window/light positions. In authentic video, face and scene illumination match. Deepfake face insertion may produce faces lit from a different direction than the scene.

3. **Shadow Consistency Verification**: Facial shadows (nose shadow, orbital shadows, chin shadow) are analyzed for mutual consistency — all shadows on the face should originate from the same light source(s). AI-generated faces may produce physically inconsistent shadow patterns where different facial features appear lit from different directions.

4. **Temporal Illumination Stability**: As the head rotates, facial shading should change smoothly and consistently with the estimated light source position. The method tracks illumination parameters across frames. Deepfakes may produce illumination that doesn't respond correctly to head pose changes — illumination remaining static during head rotation or changing independently of physical light positions.

5. **Specular-Diffuse Decomposition**: Facial skin shows both diffuse reflection (matte appearance) and specular reflection (highlights on forehead, nose, cheeks). The ratio and spatial distribution of specular-to-diffuse components should follow physical models. AI generators may produce unnatural specular patterns, absent highlights, or incorrect specular-to-diffuse ratios.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through face illumination analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Rossler, A. et al. (2019). FaceForensics++: Learning to Detect Manipulated Facial Images. ICCV.
